messages:
raj: FYI customer reported p99 regressions only on SSE streams — first-chunk arrives fast (~80ms) but there's a 800-1200ms gap before the second chunk. Non-streaming total time looks fine. customer tenant: acct-9921. Escalating for triage. :rotating_light:

jen: +1, severity P2 for now. Customer impacted in production, affects real-time chat feature. Customer says toggling to non-streaming solved it temporarily. Want repro steps and potential mitigations ASAP.

emily: @raj can you paste a minimal repro request and the exact headers they used? Are they using SSE or multipart? Any proxy in front (CDN / customer proxy)? :eyes:

raj: Repro curl they provided:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
  -H 'x-tenant-id: acct-9921'
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-7b","input":"hi"}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
Observations from their traces: first byte at ~75ms, second chunk not until ~950ms. Non-streaming HTTP POST to /v1/generate returns total ~150ms.

emily: thanks. couple hypotheses: 1) edge/stream coalescing window increased (we batch small tokens to reduce traffic) 2) KV cache warming/batching misalignment 3) intermittent application-level backpressure. Can we get edge logs for that tenant and a runtime trace for the same request id?

dave: pulled edge logs for acct-9921 around apex times, sample lines below (sanitized):
```
[edge] ts=2026-03-15T14:03:21Z tenant=acct-9921 conn_id=abc123 first_chunk=73ms chunk_count=1 coalesce_ms=300 flush_policy=adaptive
[edge] ts=2026-03-15T14:03:22Z tenant=acct-9921 conn_id=abc123 chunk_count=2 gap=920ms backend_latency=60ms
```
Looks like coalesce_ms was set to 300 but chunk gap jumped to 920ms. Need runtime side timestamps to see where the extra ~600ms went.

emily: can runtime attach token-level timing for that req id? raj, can you grab request-id header from customer logs (x-request-id) and forward? Also try a quick tenant override to disable coalescing for acct-9921:
```json
{ "tenant_overrides": { "acct-9921": { "stream_coalesce_ms": 0 } } }
```
Apply in staging per-tenant config path then repro.

raj: applied tenant override in staging and repro'd with customer payload. Results: second chunk now at ~120ms after first, p99 improved from ~1.1s to ~220ms. Customer willing to try on prod if we recommend rollout steps.

luis: for customers who can't toggle server-side, we can suggest SDK workaround to force sync response (non-streaming) as temporary: JS example: 
```js
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-open-7b', input: 'hi', stream: false });
```
Note that non-streaming increases total latency for long outputs but avoids chunk-gap jitter.

emily: good catch. Root cause likely overly aggressive chunk coalescing tuned for cost, interacts badly with small-token responses from this model+prompt pattern. Proposed mitigations:
- short term: tenant override disable coalesce for impacted tenants (what raj tested)
- mid term: make coalescing adaptive to token rate vs time (reduce coalesce_ms for small initial chunks)
- emergency: fallback to non-streaming at routing layer for tenants with repeated SSE gaps >500ms

dave: I'll add alerting rule: if SSE first-to-second-chunk gap >500ms for a tenant 1% of requests in 1h, fire critical. Also add dashboard with p95/p99 chunk-gap histogram.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by emily to canary: runtime/coalesce-fix v1.2.3 -> canary cluster (id: canary-11)

emily: canary results after 30m: no regressions, chunk-gap median dropped to 90ms for canary tenant traffic. Plan: staged rollout to 20% after smoke tests.

raj: updated customer: shared tenant-override steps and offer to flip for them now. Customer accepted a staged toggle with monitoring and will report UX. :thumbsup:

jen: next steps for support: coordinate prod tenant override for acct-9921, set expectation for 0-30min configuration window, follow up in 2 hours and close if metrics look good. Thanks team.

emily: filing followup engineering ticket to make coalescing token-aware and add per-tenant heuristics. tagging @devex for docs update on tenant overrides.

luis: I'll draft short KB for support: how to repro SSE chunk-gap, temp mitigations (tenant override, SDK non-streaming), and indicators to watch in dashboards.

raj: closing loop once customer confirms. If any hiccups ping me or drop logs here.
